text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A go-slow by air traffic controllers enters a fourth day on Tuesday.
- The government bulldozes through a motion to adjourn parliament after the opposition puts up a fight to block it and allow debate on the Public Accounts Committee report.

- Founder officials of the Labour Party of Kenya go to the High Court seeking to have the registrar-general reject an application for registration by opposition faction leader Raila Odinga and others.
- One of Raila Odinga's companies suffers a big blow when it loses a bid to purchase the multimillion shilling Kisumu molasses plant.
- Ten people are jailed for a total of 125 years for trafficking 20 tonnes of hashish worth two billion shillings.

- Opposition FORD-Kenya Chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa says Raila Odinga's expulsion from the party cannot be debated as he ceased to be a party member the day he registered as a member of the Labour Party of Kenya.
- U.S. Ambassador Prudence Bushnell hails the Kenyan government's commitment to human rights.
- The Attorney-General says the government will implement to the letter all recommendations on how to address human rights violations.
